THE READ

Energy is in a Trending phase (cycle position 72/100), above its 200-day. RS vs SPY (63d): +18.3%. Next projected peak: 2026-11.

ANALYST NOTE
CURATED 129D AGO

Energy is rolling over as of mid-2026, printing RS rank #11 -- the weakest sector -- even though it still sits #2 over the trailing window (+21.5%). The current tape is a tech/semis melt-up (SMH +67.9%, high-beta over low-vol +20.7%), and capital is rotating hard into AI growth away from the post-ceasefire oil-premium unwind: a mid-June 2026 Iran-Israel ceasefire and Hormuz-reopening expectations have drained the war-risk bid out of crude (-23.1% oil from the March 2026 peak), pulling XLE back below levels it held during the conflict. The reflation-quad backdrop (cyclicals +11.2% vs defensives +6.9%, oil +19.2% trailing) offers a re-bid scenario if the AI melt-up narrows, but a firming dollar (+3.4% DXY) and the narrow mega-cap tape suggest re-rotation is not imminent. XLE is a value/income play out of favor in a growth-led cycle phase.

Projected next peak ≈ Nov ’26 (Sep ’26–Feb ’27), from this sector’s own median half-cycle. A timing estimate, not a guarantee.
CYCLE DNA — WHY IT RHYMES
CONFIDENCE HIGH

Energy (XLE) is structurally oil-price-beta on steroids: its cycle is almost entirely determined by WTI/Brent direction, which in turn cycles through OPEC supply-policy decisions, US shale production dynamics, global growth/demand signals, and dollar direction. When oil rises in a reflation quad (cyclicals beating defensives, falling dollar, rising copper-gold), Energy almost always ranks #1 of 11 sectors. When a deflation scare, dollar surge, or supply glut crushes crude, Energy is invariably last. The sector also carries a secondary geopolitical-premium cycle layered on top: wars, sanctions, and supply-route disruptions (Hormuz, Nord Stream) cause sharp non-fundamental oil spikes that Energy equities amplify. The third axis is the opportunity-cost trade: in AI/tech melt-up tapes, Energy is starved of capital even when oil is stable because money rotates to high-growth sectors, making the sector's RS rank a function of both oil and the overall market leadership regime.

WTI/Brent crude oil price direction (primary driver ~70% of variance)
OPEC+ supply policy decisions (cuts/hikes/market-share pivots)
US shale production cycle (rig counts, break-even dynamics)
USD direction (inverse correlation -- DXY up hurts, DXY down helps)
Global growth / China demand cycle (commodity demand multiplier)
Geopolitical risk premium (wars, sanctions, supply-route threats)
TROUGHS FORM WHEN
Oil prices at multi-year lows with US rig counts declining sharply (supply destruction underway)
Energy RS rank #11 for 2+ months with record short interest in XLE/XOP (capitulation)
OPEC+ announces surprise deep cuts or geopolitical supply disruption emerges
Dollar peaks and rolls over -- DXY topping is historically bullish for crude and XLE
PEAKS FORM WHEN
Oil price reaches multi-year highs and majors' free-cash-flow yield compresses below 5% (overvaluation)
OPEC+ pivots to production increases or Saudi abandons price defense (supply catalyst)
Energy RS rank #1 sustained 3+ months in a growth/tech-led tape (exhaustion of rotation flows)
Dollar strength inflects -- DXY breaking above key levels signals commodity headwind
Median full cycle ≈ 12 months
Closest analog The current 2026 post-ceasefire selloff rhymes most closely with the 2022-11-15 leg (November 2022 to March 2023): in both cases, Energy had just completed a supply-disruption-led premium rally to #1, then reversed sharply as the catalyst faded (OPEC+ Oct 2022 cut wearing off / China-demand worry vs Iran ceasefire 2026), with money rotating hard into tech/growth (the late-2022 ChatGPT-driven AI bid in Comm/Tech mirroring the 2026 AI melt-up). In both cases Energy went from #1 to #11 in under four months, oil fell 20%+, and the broader tape was narrow/mega-cap-led. The imperfect fit: the 2022-23 reversal was compounded by an SVB credit shock, whereas the 2026 move is a cleaner geopolitical-premium drain.
